prompt: Some people think that children should not be allowed to own a smartphone until they start secondary school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
The proposal is sound and the reasoning usually offered for it is not, and the difference matters because it decides what happens on the child's eleventh birthday. The case is almost always made in terms of protection — screen time, strangers, unsuitable material — as though a smartphone were a hazard to be kept away from small children until they have grown large enough to survive it.

What that framing misses is that the difficulty is not the child's size but the device's design. A phone is not a passive object that becomes safe with maturity; it is an interface refined by continuous experimentation to capture as much attention as it possibly can, and it works on adults who understand precisely what is being done to them. Handing one to a nine-year-old is not unwise because nine-year-olds are fragile. It is unwise because nobody at any age has the willpower the arrangement quietly assumes, and a nine-year-old has not yet built the habits that partially compensate for lacking it.

That is why I would delay ownership, and equally why I am sceptical of the assumption buried in the question, that secondary school marks the point where the problem dissolves. Eleven is not a threshold of competence. It is the age at which social exclusion begins to cost more than the device does, so most families concede. Treating that concession as a graduation invites the worst possible handover: full ownership, no scaffolding, on the grounds that the child is now old enough.

So keep smartphones out of primary schools, but for the honest reason. Those years are worth protecting not because children are too young to cope, but because they are the last stretch in which sustained attention can be practised without competition. What should follow is a slow, supervised loosening, in a household where the adults are visibly subject to the same discipline they are imposing. A rule about age, on its own, relocates the problem to the following September.
title: Smartphones before secondary school
